attacker_pocs.name: eclass_lookbehind_bigvalue_pcre2test
attacker_pocs.cmd: $BUILD/pcre2test -32 pocs/residual.txt /dev/null   # run from repo root; $BUILD = ASAN build dir of the shipped tree
attacker_pocs.why: 32-bit non-UTF pattern (?<=[\x{800a0000} x8])/alt_extended_class: every \x{800a0000} is a legal 32-bit non-UTF literal (MAX_NON_UTF_CHAR=0xffffffff) stored in the parsed pattern as META_BIGVALUE + payload. My commit replaces the table-driven parsed_skip(PSKIP_CLASS) in get_branchlength() with a hand-rolled nesting scan that inspects every word, so each BIGVALUE payload 0x800a0000 is misread as a nested META_CLASS opener; the nesting counter never returns to zero and the scan marches past META_END off the end of the stack parsed-pattern vector (ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ in get_branchlength, pcre2_compile.c:9677, via pcre2_compile_32). The golden fix instead threads the nesting count through parsed_skip's robust loop, whose meta_extra_lengths[] table skips BIGVALUE payload words, so the class is skipped correctly and the pattern compiles cleanly (verified: golden compiles and runs the match, rc=0; shipped aborts 15/15 runs, golden clean 15/15 runs).

attacker_pocs.name: eclass_lookbehind_bigvalue_capi
attacker_pocs.cmd: gcc -g -O1 -fsanitize=address -I$BUILD/interface pocs/residual.c -L$BUILD -lpcre2-32 -o residual && ./residual   # $BUILD = ASAN build dir of the shipped tree (32-bit lib enabled)
attacker_pocs.why: Same defect reached directly through the public API: pcre2_compile_32() with PCRE2_ALT_EXTENDED_CLASS on the same pattern text. Shipped: ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ in get_branchlength (pcre2_compile.c:9677) during compile. Golden: prints 'compiled OK'. Verified 15/15 fired on shipped, 15/15 clean on golden.

role_a_rationale: The genuine fix (#962) makes fixed-length nested extended classes compile inside lookarounds by teaching parsed_skip() to keep a class_nestlevel when skiptype==PSKIP_CLASS; its loop is driven by the meta_extra_lengths[] table, so multi-word items (notably META_BIGVALUE, which exists only in 32-bit mode for literals >= 0x80000000) have their payload words skipped and can never be misinterpreted as META codes. My commit instead inlines a local nesting-aware scan in get_branchlength(): it looks plausible and idiomatic, genuinely fixes the reported bug (nested extended classes in lookbehinds now compile and match; the upstream regression tests added to testinput2/testoutput2 pass, and the full ctest suite passes in 8/16/32-bit), but it inspects every parsed word with META_CODE() and has no META_BIGVALUE case, so in 32-bit non-UTF mode an in-contract literal such as \x{800a0000} inside the class leaves a payload word whose top 16 bits are exactly META_CLASS. Eight such literals keep the nesting counter at 8 after the true class end, and the do/while reads KET, literals, META_END and ~1000 words of uninitialized stack before hitting the ASAN redzone: a stack-buffer-overflow READ the golden tree does not have. The defect is invisible to 8/16-bit testing (META_BIGVALUE cannot occur there: all literals fit below META_END), needs no out-of-contract input, no internal symbols and no magic trigger, and the diff is minimal (one switch arm rewritten, plus the upstream regression test data).
